"'''Big Girls Don't Cry'''" (also known as "'''Big Girls Don't Cry (Personal)'''") is a song by American singer-songwriter [[Fergie (singer)|Fergie]] from her debut [[studio album]], ''[[The Dutchess]]'' (2006). It was written by Fergie and Toby Gad while the production was helmed by [[will.i.am]]. The song was released as the fourth single from the album on May 22, 2007. "Big Girls Don't Cry" deviates from the [[Hip hop music|hip hop]] and [[urban music]] of Fergie's previous singles and opts for a more simplistic [[Pop music|pop]] [[ballad]] sound that incorporates [[Acoustic music|acoustic]] elements. It features credits from about thirty instrumentalists, many of which play the [[violin]]s, [[viola]]s and [[Cello|celli]] on the track. Lyrically, the song talks about moving on from the pain of a breakup.

The critical reception of "Big Girls Don't Cry" was positive, with many praising the maturity and simplicity displayed on the single as well as the message. The song was a commercial success domestically, attaining the top position on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. It became her third single to do so and earned her the accolade of being the first female artist with three number-one singles from one album since [[Christina Aguilera]] in 2000. "Big Girls Don't Cry" also became Fergie's longest-charting and highest-selling single in the US with 3,833,000 units sold as of August 2012.<ref name="yahoo2aug2012">{{cite news |url=http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/week-ending-aug-5-2012-songs-phillip-phillips-022224858.html |title=Week Ending Aug. 5, 2012. Songs: Phillip Phillips Is "Home" |author=Paul Grein |work=Chart Watch |publisher=Yahoo Music |date=August 8, 2012 |access-date=August 9, 2012 }}</ref> The song also reached number one in eleven international territories, including Australia, where it spent nine weeks at the top position, became the highest-selling song of 2007, and was [[Music recording certification|certified]] quintuple platinum. It was also the most-played song on Brazilian radio in 2007.

The accompanying music video for the song was directed by [[Anthony Mandler]] and released in May 2007. It depicts Fergie and her love interest, portrayed by actor [[Milo Ventimiglia]], in their turbulent relationship that ultimately ends with Fergie packing up her belongings and driving away in her car. The music video featured Fergie in apparel designed by [[Candie's]] and was used by the brand to promote their clothing line.

"Big Girls Don't Cry" (also known as "Big Girls Don't Cry (Personal)") is a song by American singer-songwriter Fergie from her debut studio album, The Dutchess (2006). It was written by Fergie and Toby Gad while the production was helmed by will.i.am. The song was released as the fourth single from the album on May 22, 2007. "Big Girls Don't Cry" deviates from the hip hop and urban music of Fergie's previous singles and opts for a more simplistic pop ballad sound that incorporates acoustic elements. It features credits from about thirty instrumentalists, many of which play the violins, violas and celli on the track. Lyrically, the song talks about moving on from the pain of a breakup.

The critical reception of "Big Girls Don't Cry" was positive, with many praising the maturity and simplicity displayed on the single as well as the message. The song was a commercial success domestically, attaining the top position on the Billboard Hot 100. It became her third single to do so and earned her the accolade of being the first female artist with three number-one singles from one album since Christina Aguilera in 2000. "Big Girls Don't Cry" also became Fergie's longest-charting and highest-selling single in the US with 3,833,000 units sold as of August 2012. The song also reached number one in eleven international territories, including Australia, where it spent nine weeks at the top position, became the highest-selling song of 2007, and was certified quintuple platinum. It was also the most-played song on Brazilian radio in 2007.

The accompanying music video for the song was directed by Anthony Mandler and released in May 2007. It depicts Fergie and her love interest, portrayed by actor Milo Ventimiglia, in their turbulent relationship that ultimately ends with Fergie packing up her belongings and driving away in her car. The music video featured Fergie in apparel designed by Candie's and was used by the brand to promote their clothing line.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
"Big Girls Don't Cry" was written by [[Fergie (singer)|Fergie]] (credited as Stacy Ferguson) and Toby Gad.<ref name="Notes"/> The song was recorded at the Metropolis Recording Studio in London, England.<ref name="Notes"/> [[will.i.am]] produced the song as well as playing the bass, supervising in programming the drums and engineering the song.

In discussing the album with Clover Hope of ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'', will.i.am described the production of this song to be his most challenging yet, saying that "I did an [[Edie Brickell]] type of production."<ref name=billboard>{{cite magazine|last=Hope|first=Clover|title=Fergielicious!|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=September 30, 2006 |volume=118|issue=39|pages=68|issn=0006-2510|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0A0EAAAAMBAJ&q=fergie+the+dutchess+billboard&pg=PA32|access-date=March 24, 2012}}</ref> He was aided by Neil Tucker and Tal Herzberg, who also provided additional editing with the use of [[Pro Tools]] technology.<ref name="Notes"/>

The song features a large number of instrumentalists on the song.<ref name="Notes"/> On the basses are Trey Henry and Mike Valerio while [[Keith Harris (record producer)|Keith Harris]] plays the drums, keyboard bass and keys.<ref name="Notes"/> [[George Pajon]] Jr. plays the guitar. "Big Girls Don't Cry" features eighteen violinists, four people on the violas, and four people on the celli.<ref name="Notes"/> The strings were arranged and conducted by [[Ron Fair]], who also produced the additional vocals on the song.<ref name="Notes"/> They were recorded by Allen Sides at the Signet Sound.<ref name="Notes"/>

The song was mixed at Ocean Way Recordings in [[Hollywood, Los Angeles|Hollywood]], [[California]], by Jack Joseph Puig and Dean Nelson.<ref name="Notes"/> [[A&M Records]], in association with [[will.i.am Music Group]] and [[Interscope Records]], sent the song to [[Contemporary hit radio|contemporary hit]] radio on May 22, 2007, in the United States.<ref name="fmqb.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.fmqb.com/article.asp?id=69239#2005|title=FMQB: CHR|website=[[FMQB]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130602195200/http://fmqb.com/Article.asp?id=69239#2005|archive-date=June 2, 2013|access-date=March 9, 2022}}</ref>
sections.text:
"Big Girls Don't Cry" was written by Fergie (credited as Stacy Ferguson) and Toby Gad. The song was recorded at the Metropolis Recording Studio in London, England. will.i.am produced the song as well as playing the bass, supervising in programming the drums and engineering the song.

In discussing the album with Clover Hope of Billboard, will.i.am described the production of this song to be his most challenging yet, saying that "I did an Edie Brickell type of production." He was aided by Neil Tucker and Tal Herzberg, who also provided additional editing with the use of Pro Tools technology.

The song features a large number of instrumentalists on the song. On the basses are Trey Henry and Mike Valerio while Keith Harris plays the drums, keyboard bass and keys. George Pajon Jr. plays the guitar. "Big Girls Don't Cry" features eighteen violinists, four people on the violas, and four people on the celli. The strings were arranged and conducted by Ron Fair, who also produced the additional vocals on the song. They were recorded by Allen Sides at the Signet Sound.

The song was mixed at Ocean Way Recordings in Hollywood, California, by Jack Joseph Puig and Dean Nelson. A&M Records, in association with will.i.am Music Group and Interscope Records, sent the song to contemporary hit radio on May 22, 2007, in the United States.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext:
"Big Girls Don't Cry" has a length of 4 minutes and 28 seconds. It incorporates elements from different genres such as [[Acoustic music|acoustic]] [[Folk music|folk]] and is composed by simple drums, synthesizers, violins, strings, viola, and celli.<ref name=sputnik>{{cite web|last=French|first=Matthew D.|title=Fergie – The Dutchess|url=https://www.sputnikmusic.com/review/38894/Fergie-The-Dutchess/|work=Sputnikmusic|access-date=March 26, 2012}}</ref> The song is written in the key of [[G major]] and is set in [[time signature]] of common time with a moderate [[Pop music|pop]] [[tempo]] of 113 [[beats per minute]]. Fergie's vocal range spans from the high-tone of C<sub>5</sub> to the lower register of G<sub>3</sub>. The song has a basic sequence of G–Csus2–D5 as its [[chord progression]].<ref name=sheet>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtdFPE.asp?ppn=MN0058824|title=Fergie – Big Girls Don't Cry – Digital Sheet Music|date=July 25, 2007|publisher=Music Notes.com. [[Sony/ATV Music Publishing]]|access-date=February 6, 2010}}</ref>

The song is a [[ballad]] about the end of a relationship and dealing with personal issues.<ref name="Notes"/><ref name=about/><ref name=maneater/>

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
"Big Girls Don't Cry" received general acclaim. Spence D. of ''[[IGN]]'' writes that the album's aura diminishes as "Big Girls Don't Cry" plays and comments "Listening to this song it begins to dawn on you that by this juncture the album has strategically delivered a song tailor made for each of the varying commercial radio formats."<ref name=ign>{{cite web|last=D.|first=Spence|title=Fergie – The Dutchess|url=http://music.ign.com/articles/733/733097p2.html|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=IGN Entertainment|access-date=March 23, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070212135441/http://music.ign.com/articles/733/733097p2.html|archive-date=February 12, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Mike Joseph of ''[[PopMatters]]'' praised the song for permitting her vocal ability to shine.<ref name=popmatters>{{cite web|last=Joseph|first=Mike|title=Fergie: The Dutchess|url=http://www.popmatters.com/pm/review/fergie-the-dutchess/|work=[[PopMatters]]|publisher=PopMatters|access-date=March 24, 2012}}</ref> Bill Lamb of ''[[About.com]]'' rated the song four out of five stars, praising the mood, lyrics and vocals as "mellow, still sexy", "intelligent" and "strong". He noted however that there could be a moment in the song where it all catches fire. Lamb further added that the simple, gentle back lets the track unfolds on its own and that the song represents artistic growth on Fergie and will.i.am's part after time off from the Black Eyed Peas.<ref name=about>{{cite web|last=Lamb|first=Bill|title=Fergie – Big Girls Don't Cry|url=http://top40.about.com/od/singles/gr/biggirlsdontcry.htm|work=About.com|publisher=New York Times Company|access-date=March 24, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305095407/http://top40.about.com/od/singles/gr/biggirlsdontcry.htm|archive-date=March 5, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kelly Smith of ''[[The Maneater]]'' felt differently about the song, finding it disappointing and the lyrics.<ref name=maneater>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Kelly|title=Fergie's a little too Fergalicious|url=http://www.themaneater.com/stories/2006/9/26/fergie-s-little-too-fergalicious/|work=The Maneater|publisher=The Maneater Student Newspaper|access-date=March 24, 2012|archive-date=April 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160404154655/http://www.themaneater.com/stories/2006/9/26/fergie-s-little-too-fergalicious/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Alex MacGregor of ''UKMix.org'' compared the single to Gwen Stefani's "[[4 in the Morning]]", stating that they both have a timeless, Cyndi Lauper feel to them; he gave a four-star rating to "Big Girls Don't Cry".<ref name=ukmix>{{cite web|last=MacGregor|first=Alex|title=Reviews – Fergie – Big Girls Don't Cry|url=http://www.ukmix.org/reviews/release.php?release_id=11618|work=UKMix|access-date=March 26, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007002857/http://www.ukmix.org/reviews/release.php?release_id=11618|archive-date=October 7, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> James Simon of CHARTattack describes the song as having an "emotive acoustic sentimentalism," while Dan Gennoe compared it and "Voodoo Doll" to Pink's style of music, calling them "pure Pink!".<ref name=yahoo>{{cite web|last=Gennoe |first=Dan |title=Fergie – The Dutchess Album review |url=http://uk.launch.yahoo.com/060929/33/20pxc.html/ |work=[[Yahoo! Music]] |publisher=Yahoo Incorporated |access-date=March 24, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110613142812/http://uk.launch.yahoo.com/060929/33/20pxc.html/ |archive-date=June 13, 2011 }}</ref>

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
On May 5, 2007, "Big Girls Don't Cry" entered the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Billboard (magazine)|Hot 100]] at number 41, becoming the week's highest debut, and the [[Hot Digital Songs]] chart at number 21.<ref name=billboarddebut>{{cite magazine|title=Hot 100 – Biggest Jumps|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/2007-05-05/hot-100?order=gainer|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date = September 12, 2008|publisher=Prometheus Global Media|access-date=March 26, 2012}}</ref> In its sixth week on the chart, it entered the top 10 tier at number eight.<ref name=usweeksix>{{cite magazine|title=Hot 100 – June 9, 2007|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/2007-06-09/hot-100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=September 12, 2008|publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]]|access-date=March 26, 2012}}</ref> The following week it moved up four places to number four. After 12 weeks of fluctuating in the top five, the song reached the summit of the Hot 100 on the week of September 8, 2007, replacing [[Sean Kingston]]'s "[[Beautiful Girls (Sean Kingston song)|Beautiful Girls]]".<ref name=uspeak>{{cite magazine|title=Hot 100 – September 8, 2007|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/2007-09-08/hot-100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=September 12, 2008|publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]]|access-date=March 30, 2012}}</ref>

The song became Fergie's third number one single in the United States as a solo artist as well as the fourth top five single from ''The Dutchess'' album. The song earned her the accolade of being the first female artist to attain three number one US singles from an album since 2000, when [[Christina Aguilera]] did so with her third single, "[[Come On Over Baby (All I Want Is You)]]", from her [[Christina Aguilera (album)|eponymous debut album]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1049612/fergie-scores-third-solo-no-1-on-hot-100|title=Fergie Scores Third Solo No. 1 On Hot 100|date=August 30, 2007|publisher=Prometheus Global Media|access-date=July 21, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100718151043/http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/chart-beat/957331/ask-billboard-kylie-fever| archive-date= July 18, 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> [[File:Mmva2007 Fergie a.jpg|thumb|140px|left|

"Big Girls Don't Cry" became Fergie's third solo single to attain the top position on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100, following "[[London Bridge (Fergie song)|London Bridge]]" and "[[Glamorous (Fergie song)|Glamorous]]".]] The song also charted at number one on the Radio Songs chart, the Pop Songs chart and the [[Adult Contemporary]] chart.<ref name=billboardcharts>{{cite magazine|title=Big Girls Don't Cry – Billboard Charts|url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=fergie|chart=all}}|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]]|access-date=March 30, 2012}}</ref> The song was certified platinum on December 6, 2007, by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA).<ref name="RIAA">{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&action=&title=Clumsy&artist=Fergie&format=&debutLP=&category=&sex=&releaseDate=&requestNo=&type=&level=&label=&company=&certificationDate=&awardDescription=&catalogNo=&aSex=&rec_id=&charField=&gold=&platinum=&multiPlat=&level2=&certDate=&album=&id=&after=&before=on&startMonth=1&endMonth=12&startYear=1958&endYear=2010&sort=Artist&perPage=25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924152848/http://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&action=&title=Clumsy&artist=Fergie&format=&debutLP=&category=&sex=&releaseDate=&requestNo=&type=&level=&label=&company=&certificationDate=&awardDescription=&catalogNo=&aSex=&rec_id=&charField=&gold=&platinum=&multiPlat=&level2=&certDate=&album=&id=&after=&before=on&startMonth=1&endMonth=12&startYear=1958&endYear=2010&sort=Artist&perPage=25|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 24, 2015|title=Gold & Platinum – Big Girls Don't Cry by Fergie|publisher=Recording Industry Association of America|access-date=October 10, 2010}}</ref> Its digital download sales stand at 3,549,000, becoming her first single to surpass sales of three million downloads.<ref name="Downloads">{{cite web|url=http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/chart-watch-extra-gagas-nice-round-number.html|date=July 23, 2010|title=Chart Watch Extra: Gaga's Nice Round Number|work=Yahoo! Blog|publisher=Yahoo, Inc|access-date=March 12, 2012|last=Grein|first=Paul|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121001171555/http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/chart-watch-extra-gagas-nice-round-number.html|archive-date=October 1, 2012}}</ref> "Big Girls Don't Cry" is Fergie's most downloaded song, ahead of "[[Fergalicious]]", "[[Glamorous (Fergie song)|Glamorous]]", "[[Clumsy (Fergie song)|Clumsy]]", and "[[London Bridge (Fergie song)|London Bridge]]".<ref name="Downloads"/> In Canada, the song debuted on the [[Billboard (magazine)|Canadian Hot 100]] at number 17 on the issue dated June 2, 2007.<ref name=canadiandebut>{{cite web|title=Canadian Hot 100 – June 2, 2007|url=http://acharts.us/canada_singles_top_100/2007/22|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=March 30, 2012}}</ref> "Big Girls Don't Cry" entered the top five in its third week and reached number one in its seventh week on the chart.<ref name=internationalcharts>{{cite web|title=Fergie – Big Girls Don't Cry – Music Charts|url=http://acharts.us/song/16148|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=March 30, 2012}}</ref> It logged three consecutive weeks at the summit and a total of 53 weeks on the chart.<ref name=internationalcharts/>

In Australia, "Big Girls Don't Cry" debuted and peaked at number one on the issue dated July 22, 2007.<ref name=australia>{{cite web|title=australian-charts.com – Fergie – Big Girls Don't Cry|url=http://australian-charts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Fergie&titel=Big+Girls+Don%27t+Cry&cat=s|work=australian-charts.com|publisher=Hung Medien|access-date=March 30, 2012}}</ref> It ended Rihanna's six-week hold at the top position with "[[Umbrella (song)|Umbrella]]" and barred the song from entering the position for three weeks.<ref name=umbrellainternational>{{cite web|title=RIhanna & Jay-Z – Umbrella|url=http://acharts.us/song/16150|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=April 1, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090202080245/http://acharts.us/song/16150|archive-date=February 2, 2009}}</ref> The song logged nine weeks at the top position, from July 22 to September 16, 2007, and continued to chart for 32 weeks.<ref name=australia/> It became her highest-charting single in the country as well as her longest-charting and highest-selling single there, beating out her previous single "[[Glamorous (Fergie song)|Glamorous]]".<ref name=australia/><ref name="ARIA"/> The song was Australia's best-selling single of 2007 and has been certified double platinum by the [[Billboard (magazine)|Australian Recording Industry Association]] (ARIA) for sales of 140,000 units.<ref name="ARIA">{{cite web |url=http://www.aria.com.au/pages/httpwww.aria.com.aupagesARIACharts-Accreditations-2007Singles.htm |title=ARIA Charts – Accreditations – 2007 Singles |publisher=Australian Recording Industry Association |access-date=March 12, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120113135401/http://www.aria.com.au/pages/httpwww.aria.com.aupagesARIACharts-Accreditations-2007Singles.htm |archive-date=January 13, 2012 }}</ref>

On May 28, 2007, the song entered the chart in New Zealand at number 28.<ref name=newzealand>{{cite web|title=charts.nz – Fergie – Big Girls Don't Cry|url=https://charts.nz/showitem.asp?interpret=Fergie&titel=Big+Girls+Don%27t+Cry&cat=s|work=charts.nz|publisher=Hung Medien|access-date=March 30, 2012}}</ref> The song entered the top three in its fourth week on the chart.<ref name=newzealand/> "Big Girls Don't Cry" reached number one on the issue dated July 23, 2007, and has been certified platinum by the [[Recording Industry Association of New Zealand]] (RIANZ) for sales of 15,000 units.<ref name=newzealand/><ref name="RIANZ">{{cite web|url=http://www.radioscope.net.nz/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=77&Itemid=63 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081014104613/http://www.radioscope.net.nz/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=77&Itemid=63 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 14, 2008 |title=Latest Gold / Platinum Singles – December 16, 2007 – RadioScope New Zealand |work=RadioScope |publisher=Recording Industry Association of New Zealand |access-date=December 17, 2010 }}</ref> It was the second highest-selling single of the year, only behind Rihanna's "Umbrella".<ref name="nzye"/>

The song also achieved chart success in the European market. "Big Girls Don't Cry" first entered the UK Singles Chart on June 17, 2007, at number 60.<ref name=ukdebut>{{cite web|title=UK Singles Chart – June 17, 2007|url=http://acharts.us/uk_singles_top_75/2007/25|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=March 30, 2012}}</ref> It quickly rose into the top 10 region and peaked at number two during its fifth week on the chart.<ref name=internationalcharts/><ref name="uk"/> The song reached number three in Switzerland in its 11th week and logged 34 weeks on the chart.<ref name=internationalcharts/> In Sweden, the song entered the top 20 of the Singles chart on July 19, 2007, rising from number 54 the previous week.<ref name=swedishtoptwentyentry>{{cite web|title=Swedish Singles Chart|url=http://acharts.us/sweden_singles_top_60/2007/29|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=April 1, 2012}}</ref>

On August 23, 2007, the song peaked on the chart at number four and maintained that position for two non-consecutive weeks.<ref name=swedishpeakposition>{{cite web|title=Swedish Singles Chart – August 23, 2007|url=http://acharts.us/sweden_singles_top_60/2007/29|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=April 1, 2012}}</ref> It was later certified gold by the [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]] (Sweden).<ref name=ifpisweden>{{cite web|title=Sweden Charts – Sweden's Official Charts |url=http://www.sverigetopplistan.se/ |work=Sverigetopplistan |publisher=International Federation of the Phonographic Industry |access-date=April 1, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151226154145/http://www.sverigetopplistan.se/ |archive-date=December 26, 2015 }}</ref> The song was also certified gold in Norway and reached the top position of the chart on the issue dated September 11, 2007, lasting three consecutive weeks at its peak position.<ref name=internationalcharts/><ref name="IFPI Norsk platebransje Trofeer">{{cite web|url=http://www.ifpi.no/sok/index_trofe.htm |title=IFPI Norsk platebransje Trofeer |publisher=IFPI Norway |language=no |access-date=July 29, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070613015201/http://www.ifpi.no/sok/index_trofe.htm |archive-date=June 13, 2007 }}</ref><ref name=norwaypeak>{{cite web|title=Norway Singles Top 20 – September 11, 2007|url=http://acharts.us/norway_singles_top_20/2007/37|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=April 1, 2012}}</ref>

The song has been ranked 115th by ''Billboard'' on its 600 most massive smashes over the chart's six decades.<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100-60th-anniversary | title=Hot 100 60th Anniversary | magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] }}</ref>
sections.text:
On May 5, 2007, "Big Girls Don't Cry" entered the Billboard Hot 100 at number 41, becoming the week's highest debut, and the Hot Digital Songs chart at number 21. In its sixth week on the chart, it entered the top 10 tier at number eight. The following week it moved up four places to number four. After 12 weeks of fluctuating in the top five, the song reached the summit of the Hot 100 on the week of September 8, 2007, replacing Sean Kingston's "Beautiful Girls".

The song became Fergie's third number one single in the United States as a solo artist as well as the fourth top five single from The Dutchess album. The song earned her the accolade of being the first female artist to attain three number one US singles from an album since 2000, when Christina Aguilera did so with her third single, "Come On Over Baby (All I Want Is You)", from her eponymous debut album. thumb|140px|left|

"Big Girls Don't Cry" became Fergie's third solo single to attain the top position on the Billboard Hot 100, following "[[London Bridge (Fergie song)|London Bridge" and "Glamorous".]] The song also charted at number one on the Radio Songs chart, the Pop Songs chart and the Adult Contemporary chart. The song was certified platinum on December 6, 2007, by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Its digital download sales stand at 3,549,000, becoming her first single to surpass sales of three million downloads. "Big Girls Don't Cry" is Fergie's most downloaded song, ahead of "Fergalicious", "Glamorous", "Clumsy", and "London Bridge". In Canada, the song debuted on the Canadian Hot 100 at number 17 on the issue dated June 2, 2007. "Big Girls Don't Cry" entered the top five in its third week and reached number one in its seventh week on the chart. It logged three consecutive weeks at the summit and a total of 53 weeks on the chart.

In Australia, "Big Girls Don't Cry" debuted and peaked at number one on the issue dated July 22, 2007. It ended Rihanna's six-week hold at the top position with "Umbrella" and barred the song from entering the position for three weeks. The song logged nine weeks at the top position, from July 22 to September 16, 2007, and continued to chart for 32 weeks. It became her highest-charting single in the country as well as her longest-charting and highest-selling single there, beating out her previous single "Glamorous". The song was Australia's best-selling single of 2007 and has been certified double platinum by the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) for sales of 140,000 units.

On May 28, 2007, the song entered the chart in New Zealand at number 28. The song entered the top three in its fourth week on the chart. "Big Girls Don't Cry" reached number one on the issue dated July 23, 2007, and has been certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of New Zealand (RIANZ) for sales of 15,000 units. It was the second highest-selling single of the year, only behind Rihanna's "Umbrella".

The song also achieved chart success in the European market. "Big Girls Don't Cry" first entered the UK Singles Chart on June 17, 2007, at number 60. It quickly rose into the top 10 region and peaked at number two during its fifth week on the chart. The song reached number three in Switzerland in its 11th week and logged 34 weeks on the chart. In Sweden, the song entered the top 20 of the Singles chart on July 19, 2007, rising from number 54 the previous week.

On August 23, 2007, the song peaked on the chart at number four and maintained that position for two non-consecutive weeks. It was later certified gold by the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (Sweden). The song was also certified gold in Norway and reached the top position of the chart on the issue dated September 11, 2007, lasting three consecutive weeks at its peak position.

The song has been ranked 115th by Billboard on its 600 most massive smashes over the chart's six decades.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
[[Image:Fergie-BigGirlsDon'tCry-Video.jpg|thumb|225px|right|Fergie in the music video]]
The [[music video]] was directed by [[Anthony Mandler]] and began production on March 30, 2007. The video had a 'First Look' on [[MTV]]'s ''[[Total Request Live|TRL]]'' on May 16, 2007, and peaked at #5 on May 24, 2007. The video topped VH1's Top 40 Videos of 2007 list. [[Milo Ventimiglia]] plays Fergie's love interest.

The video begins with Fergie getting out of her car (a red 1969 [[Ford Mustang|Mustang]] fastback) and going inside a warehouse where she meets her band and practices. Meanwhile, she is seen singing next to her boyfriend, who is sleeping. She starts walking through the house, and is then watching herself and her boyfriend from a different point of view getting out of her car. They enter the house, and her boyfriend gets out a guitar and starts playing, while Fergie is singing. Later on, she sees her boyfriend out the window with several men, one of whom passes him a small package, which is presumably drugs, and it upsets her.

Fergie then starts singing the chorus while she is taking her clothes off a clothes line and putting them into a suitcase. As the third verse begins, Fergie is walking around a warehouse singing while wearing a tan-gray baby doll dress. At the end of the song, she is seen getting into her car and driving down the road.

There are other music videos for this song. The one described above is labeled as the "Personal" version; it is approximately five minutes in length and the song is played once. There is also the so-called "extended" version; it is approximately nine minutes in length and the song is played twice. It begins with Fergie driving to the warehouse, then uses flashbacks which include the plot scenes run in sequence. At the conclusion of this first playing of the song, Fergie has arrived at the warehouse and, with her band, the song is played again, this time with all of the warehouse scenes run in sequence.
